subject: Custom SLA exhibit & order form language - redline from CloudMed
messages:
From: Elena Vargas <elena@cloudmed.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudmed.com, trevor.sims@cloudmed.com
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Custom SLA addendum - initial redline attached

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week — the Redwood runtime looks promising for our telemetry-driven workflows. Before procurement can move forward we need two small but critical additions to the MSA/SOW:

1) An availability exhibit that codifies regional availability targets and a clear credit schedule for multi-region failovers.
2) Order form language that allows a limited availability exception for our hybrid on-prem connector during peak-batch windows, with documented mitigations and runbook commitments.

I've attached a redline (CloudMed_SLA_Addendum_Redline_20290415.docx) with suggested language. High level asks: 99.95% monthly uptime for US prod (applies across hosted + dedicated), and explicit latency SLOs for 95th/99th token latency for interactive routes.

Who on your side will own operations evidence/telemetry mapping? Procurement will need an ops contact and an expected evidence delivery schedule.

Elena Vargas
Dir, Cloud Integrations
CloudMed Solutions

Attachment: CloudMed_SLA_Addendum_Redline_20290415.docx (docx)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Vargas <elena@cloudmed.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, david_kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 08:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Custom SLA addendum - initial redline attached

Elena — thanks for the clear redline and the target SLOs. Attaching an internal draft response that addresses language we can accept vs. items that require an operational runbook or product changes (see redwood_sla_response_draft_20290416.docx).

Quick answers up front:
- We can commit to a 99.95% monthly availability for the Hosted service in the US region, with the caveat that hybrid on-prem connectors are scoped as an exception in the exhibit (we propose language to capture "connector-induced downtime" and mitigation steps).
- We can provide 95th and 99th percentile token latency SLOs for interactive routes for the dedicated-hosted combo, but need to finalize measurement windows and exact request classes (e.g., "interactive single-turn" vs "streaming chat").

Action items / asks from CloudMed so we can finalize the exhibit: 
- Procurement: confirm acceptance of proposed credit schedule in the attached response.
- Ops: please share a sample traffic profile (peak TPS and typical sequence lengths) so our SREs can validate the latency buckets.
- Legal: any hard requirement to include KV-cache-level guarantees (we typically avoid implementation-level guarantees in the MSA) — call this out if needed.

Proposing a 30-minute alignment call tomorrow at 10:00am PT to walk the redline and agree on the measurement definitions. I'll be on the call with Karthik (SRE) and David (Legal).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_sla_response_draft_20290416.docx (docx)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Elena Vargas <elena@cloudmed.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Apr 2029 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Custom SLA addendum - initial redline attached

Elena / team — quick technical note ahead of our call. High level: operationally this is feasible but there are a few constraints to call out in the exhibit language. Proposed fallback wording included below and I'll bring a 1-page runbook summary to the meeting.

Feasibility notes:
- 99.95% monthly availability in-hosted (US): OK. We will include our regional failover flow and expected RTOs (regional switch completed within X minutes for user-facing endpoints).
- Latency SLOs for interactive routes: achievable for typical single-turn generation (<= 95th percentile at ~120ms token latency in our tests for median sequence lengths). 99th percentile will vary with sequence length — we recommend defining SLOs per request class and capping maximum sequence length for the SLO to apply.
- Hybrid on-prem connector: we cannot commit to end-to-end uptime for customer-owned connectors. Recommend: exhibit language that classifies connector interruptions as "Customer-side exceptions" and ties Redwood obligations to our documented mitigations (retries, local batching, caching TTLs).

Suggested exhibit snippet (summary):
- "Availability SLOs apply to Redwood-managed endpoints and infrastructure. For hybrid connector architectures, availability exceptions caused by Customer-managed components are excluded from Redwood service credits provided Redwood has completed all documented mitigation steps."

I'll attach our ops summary (ops-runbook-summary_20290416.pdf) to the call.

Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
Attachment: ops-runbook-summary_20290416.pdf (pdf)

From: Elena Vargas <elena@cloudmed.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: trevor.sims@cloudmed.com, procurement@cloudmed.com
Date: Wed, 17 Apr 2029 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Custom SLA addendum - initial redline attached

Kimberly / Karthik — thanks, that framing helps.

On Tue, Apr 16, 2029 at 11:05 AM karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Elena / team — quick technical note ahead of our call. High level: operationally this is feasible but there are a few constraints to call out in the exhibit language. Proposed fallback wording included below and I'll bring a 1-page runbook summary to the meeting.

We reviewed the proposed snippet internally and procurement is OK with classifying connector incidents as "Customer-side exceptions" provided Redwood commits to:
- publishing an operations evidence packet within 5 business days of any incident that affects more than 0.5% of monthly requests, and
- a templated mitigation checklist that our on-call can follow to narrow down whether the disruption is connector-side vs Redwood-side.

We can proceed on the 10:00am PT call tomorrow — if you can circulate the redwood_sla_response_draft_20290416.docx and the ops-runbook-summary_20290416.pdf ahead of the meeting that would be ideal. Also please send the DocuSign route when you have the final exhibit language so procurement can sign quickly.

Regards,
Elena Vargas
Dir, Cloud Integrations
CloudMed Solutions

Links: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/abcdef123456
